The Palace of Peace and Reconciliation is a 62 metre pyramid of steel, stone and glass in Astana, the capital of Kazakhstan, designed by Norman Foster's firm and finished in 2006. It was built to house the Congress of World Religions and serves as a spiritual centre for no single faith, and a hall for events.

Its height equals the width of its base. Inside are an opera hall at the bottom, meeting rooms, and at the top an apex of stained glass by the artist Brian Clarke, with doves flying across a sky of blue and gold. The idea is a building where all faiths meet as equals.

It is one of the showpieces of the new capital built after Astana became the capital in 1997, with which Nazarbayev meant to give the young state a modern face. Foster's firm also designed the Khan Shatyr nearby, a giant tent-shaped shopping centre.
